items.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Gibson’s jazz party, he’s the granddaddy of jazz parties, he invented the jazz party.

ctx.x: Just a word about this phenomenon of these jazz festivals, these jazz parties, it’s like a great thing for musicians.

It is a great thing. This one’s been going on here in Scottsdale for sixteen or eighteen years. Some of them have dropped by the wayside unfortunately. There were so many of them just a few years ago, let’s say about five, ten years ago there were so many jazz parties all around the country, that a lot of people who wanted to go and hear this one, then wanted to go and hear that one, then wanted to go and hear that one, they couldn’t afford it or some of the parties would overlap and the producers, the promoters…

And then there’s a couple of other parties around the country that have hung on for 10 or 15 years and struggled as hard as they could and have done well but then finally just said no, we just can’t do any more, we have to cancel, you know for whatever reason. But thank God there’s still a number of these wonderful parties around the country that we get a chance to play at. And I get a chance to I think maybe if you ask some of the other guys they’ll tell you the same thing, we get a chance to see each other…
